46311.e: The Northern Ireland conflict, also called “The Troubles”, claimed over 3,500 lives from the late 1960s onwards. The agreement created a political framework for peace.
46311.m: The Good Friday Agreement ended the Northern Ireland conflict.

46312.q: In which city was the Good Friday Agreement signed on 10 April 1998?
46312.e: That is why the agreement is also called the Belfast Agreement. It was concluded on Good Friday after long negotiations through the night.
46312.m: The Good Friday Agreement is also called the Belfast Agreement.

46313.q: Under the Good Friday Agreement, what were the paramilitary groups supposed to do with their weapons?
46313.e: The agreement provided for weapons to be put completely beyond use, called “decommissioning”. The IRA completed this step in 2005.
46313.m: After 1998 the paramilitaries were to give up all their weapons.

46314.q: Which joint body for Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland did the Good Friday Agreement create?
46314.e: In the North/South Ministerial Council, ministers from both sides work together in areas such as transport or tourism. A British-Irish Council was also set up.
46314.m: The North/South Ministerial Council links Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.

46315.q: What did the Good Friday Agreement provide for convicted members of paramilitary groups that kept to the ceasefire?
46315.e: Prisoners from groups that kept to the ceasefire were to be released early within two years. This point was especially controversial for victims' families.
46315.m: The Good Friday Agreement provided for the early release of prisoners.

46316.q: Which change to its constitution did the Republic of Ireland make as part of the Good Friday Agreement?
a: It gave up its territorial claim to Northern Ireland
It abolished the office of president
46316.e: Articles 2 and 3 of the Irish constitution had previously claimed the whole island. They were changed so that unification is only possible with the consent of a majority in both parts.
46316.m: In 1998 Ireland gave up its constitutional claim to Northern Ireland.

46317.q: Which principle of government did the Good Friday Agreement create for Northern Ireland?
46317.e: Unionists and nationalists must both be represented in the regional government. Important decisions need the agreement of both communities.
46317.m: Since 1998 Northern Ireland has been governed on the principle of power-sharing.

46318.q: Which right regarding nationality does the Good Friday Agreement guarantee to the people of Northern Ireland?
a: To be British, Irish or both
46318.e: Everyone born in Northern Ireland may identify as British, Irish or both. Accordingly, they can hold both nationalities.
46318.m: In Northern Ireland you may be British, Irish or both.

46319.q: In which city were peace negotiations between Colombia and the FARC held between 2012 and 2016?
46319.e: The talks took place in the Cuban capital. Cuba and Norway acted as guarantor states.
46319.m: Colombia and the FARC negotiated in Havana.

46320.q: What happened in the referendum of 2 October 2016 on the first peace agreement with the FARC?
46320.e: About 50.2 per cent voted no. The agreement was then renegotiated and a new version was approved by Congress in November 2016.
46320.m: The first peace agreement with the FARC narrowly failed at the ballot box in 2016.

46321.q: Which Colombian president received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2016 for the peace process with the FARC?
46321.e: Juan Manuel Santos received the prize shortly after the failed referendum. The committee wanted to strengthen the peace process with it.
46321.m: Juan Manuel Santos received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2016 for peace in Colombia.

46322.q: Since which year had the FARC guerrillas been fighting against the Colombian state?
46322.e: The FARC grew out of peasant self-defence groups in 1964. The conflict was one of the longest armed conflicts in the Americas.

46323.q: Who monitored the handing over of weapons by FARC fighters in 2017?
a: The Organization of American States alone
46323.e: A political mission of the United Nations collected and registered the weapons. The handover was completed in June 2017.
46323.m: The UN monitored the disarmament of the FARC.

46324.q: What is the special court that deals with crimes from the conflict in the peace process called?
46324.e: The Special Jurisdiction for Peace, in Spanish JEP, is an instrument of transitional justice. Those who tell the truth and compensate victims can receive milder sentences.
46324.m: The Special Jurisdiction for Peace deals with the crimes of the conflict.

46325.q: What did the FARC become after the peace agreement of 2016?
a: A new guerrilla group in Venezuela
46325.e: The FARC laid down its weapons and became a political party. The agreement guaranteed it seats in Congress for some years.
46325.m: After the peace agreement the FARC turned into a party.

46326.q: In which city did the Indochina Conference take place in 1954?
46326.e: The conference met in Geneva from 26 April to 21 July 1954. Once again Switzerland provided a neutral place for negotiations.
46326.m: The Indochina Conference took place in Geneva in 1954.

46327.q: Which military defeat of France came immediately before the Indochina Conference?
a: The Battle of Điện Biên Phủ
46327.e: The French fortress of Điện Biên Phủ fell on 7 May 1954, while the conference was already under way. This greatly weakened France's negotiating position.
46327.m: The fall of Điện Biên Phủ shaped the Indochina Conference.
